questions.stem: Where does fertilisation normally take place?

options.text: In the fallopian tube (oviduct)
In the vagina
In the ovary
In the uterus

questions.explanation: Fertilisation normally takes place in the fallopian tube (oviduct), usually in the upper third nearest the ovary. Sperm travel from the vagina through the uterus to reach the egg in the fallopian tube.

questions.stem: What is the role of the acrosome during fertilisation?

options.text: It attracts the sperm towards the egg
It carries the genetic material of the sperm
It releases enzymes that digest through the egg's protective layer
It provides energy for the sperm to swim

questions.explanation: The acrosome is a cap-like structure at the tip of the sperm head. It releases digestive enzymes that break down the protective jelly layer (zona pellucida) surrounding the egg, allowing the sperm to penetrate and fuse with the egg.

questions.stem: What is the cell called that is formed when a sperm fuses with an egg?

options.text: A gamete
A zygote
An embryo
A fetus

questions.explanation: When a sperm and egg fuse, the resulting cell is called a zygote. It contains the full set of 46 chromosomes (23 from each parent). The zygote then begins dividing by mitosis to form an embryo.

options.text: The division of the zygote into two cells
The embedding of the embryo into the uterus lining
The release of an egg from the ovary
The fusion of sperm and egg

questions.explanation: Implantation is when the developing embryo (a ball of cells called a blastocyst) embeds itself into the thick, blood-rich lining of the uterus. This usually occurs about 6-7 days after fertilisation and is the start of pregnancy.

questions.stem: How many chromosomes does a human zygote contain?
questions.explanation: A human zygote contains 46 chromosomes (23 pairs). The sperm contributes 23 chromosomes and the egg contributes 23 chromosomes, restoring the diploid number when they fuse during fertilisation.

questions.stem: What prevents more than one sperm from fertilising an egg?

options.text: The egg moves away after one sperm enters
The egg's membrane and jelly layer change to block other sperm
Only one sperm is ever released
The remaining sperm are destroyed by white blood cells

questions.explanation: After the first sperm penetrates the egg, the zona pellucida (jelly layer) and cell membrane undergo rapid changes that prevent any other sperm from entering. This ensures the zygote has the correct number of chromosomes.

questions.stem: What type of cell division does the zygote undergo as it travels towards the uterus?

options.text: Meiosis
Budding
Binary fission
Mitosis

questions.explanation: The zygote divides repeatedly by mitosis as it travels along the fallopian tube towards the uterus. This produces a ball of genetically identical cells. It takes about 6-7 days to reach the uterus and implant.
